input.quote: 14.2.2 At-Will Termination by PB. PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
input.rationale: Section 14.2.2 is PB's only at-will exit, and it fails the fallback on material terms: it is unavailable until SFJ has paid or incurred $60 million of Development Costs, it closes entirely once the first Regulatory Approval is received, and the notice figure is left blank ([***]) rather than set within the 60-90 day band. In a multi-year development term that is not a usable customer convenience right. The redline restores it as an express termination "for convenience, without cause, at any time" on thirty (30) days' prior written notice, adds a pro rata refund of PB's prepayments (broadened from "fees" because this Agreement uses Approval Payments and Buy-Out Payment rather than a defined fee concept), and states that SFJ has no convenience termination right during the Term. SFJ's exits (14.2.3 MAE, 14.2.5 bankruptcy, 14.2.6 Change of Control, 14.2.7 safety, 14.2.8.1 compliance breach, 14.2.9 Adverse Patent Impact, 14.2.10 JSC decision) are each trigger-based rather than at-will, so we do not flag them as vendor convenience rights; the new sentence confirms that reading. We target the preferred level because the fallback's three-months-of-fees cap has no analogue here: the retained 300% Development Cost payment is consideration for purchasing the Trial Data Package under Section 11.1.1.4, not a subscription penalty, and we leave those economics and the ARTICLE 6 carry-over untouched. Residual commercial points for negotiation (noted, not redlined): the exit is unconditional but not free, and 14.2.10 is close to discretionary in practice.

proposal.summary: Give PB an express unconditional right to terminate for convenience/without cause on 30 days' written notice with pro rata refund of prepayments, and bar SFJ convenience termination during the Term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need a clear, unconditional customer exit: as drafted PB's at-will right only opens after SFJ has spent $60 million, closes at first Regulatory Approval, and leaves the notice period blank. We have made it an express termination for convenience without cause on thirty (30) days' written notice with a pro rata refund of PB's prepayments, and confirmed SFJ has no convenience termination right during the Term.

ops.oldText: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
ops.newText: PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause, at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ, and SFJ will refund pro rata any fees or other amounts prepaid by PB for the period after the effective date of termination. SFJ has no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Term.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
